newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end down in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end down in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index closed down in slow trade on Wednesday on a continuation of Tuesday's correction with a wait-and-see attitude dominating the market, traders said.
The index edged down 0.368 points or 0.59 percent to 62.013 points, on volume of 11.9 million shares worth $5.4 million against $7.0 million on Tuesday.
Brokers said selling focused on shares likely to post poor 1996 results, while some institutional support for property developer Lujiazui prevented the index from falling further.

"The index did not fall sharply today thanks to institutional support for Lujiazui, but it is likely to fall further in the short term due to expectations of poor results for most of the B share firms," one broker said.
Lujiazui was today's second most active share, up $0.012 or 1.50 percent to $0.808 on volume of 2.0 million shares.
Of 43 B shares, 40 traded, with 27 down, four flat and nine up.
Industrial Sewing Machine was the biggest loser on talk of poor 1996 results, plunging $0.018 or 10 percent to its limit-down of $0.162 on volume of 30,000 shares.
Clothing maker Shanghai Kaikai was again the most active stock on profit-taking, falling $0.004 or 1.16 percent $0.338 on volume of 2.6 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index closed down on a technical rebound after sharp losses yesterday, but the potential for further rises is limited with market sentiment unstable, brokers said.

The A index rose 9.698 points or 1.02 percent to 956.959 points on volume of 174.1 million shares worth 1.6 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index closed up 19.546 points or 0.81 percent to 2428.329 points.
Trading company Liaoning Chengda was the star on institutional buying, rising 1.29 yuan or 7.87 percent to 17.68 yuan on volume of 1.3 million shares.
